name: Prosecutorial incentives

subjectOf.text: Once prosecutors have investigated and identified corporate wrongdoing, non and deferred prosecution agreements let them avoid an expensive trial against a sophisticated and well funded corporate defendant, which is one reason both sides have strong incentives to settle.
subjectOf.abstract: prosecutors have investigated and identified corporate wrongdoing, they can use N/DPAs to avoid an expensive trial against a sophisticated and well-funded cor- porate defendant.
subjectOf.citation: Wulf A. Kaal, Timothy Lacine, The Effect of Deferred and Non-Prosecution Agreements on Corporate Governance Evidence from 1993-20 (2014). SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=2486570

subjectOf.text: Prosecutors favor non and deferred prosecution agreements because those agreements avoid the uncertainty of potentially catastrophic collateral consequences for the company, unlike an indictment.
subjectOf.abstract: Second, prosecutors favor N/DPAs because they do not entail the uncertainty of potentially catastrophic collateral consequences for the company.
subjectOf.citation: Wulf A. Kaal, Timothy Lacine, The Effect of Deferred and Non-Prosecution Agreements on Corporate Governance Evidence from 1993-20 (2014). SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=2486570
